Scope: every non-prose path of the diff — `packages/lint/src/aggregate-pair-verdict.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.test.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-sortable-fields.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-sortable-fields.test.ts` (the changeset `.changeset/32449-aggregate-door-pairs-refused-at-authoring.md` read for ② and ④ in round 3, byte-identical here) + the cited files, checked at this head for change since round 3 — `packages/spec/src/ui/view-grouping-query.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/aggregate-field-type-compatibility.ts`, `packages/objectql/**`, `packages/lint/**`, `ui/**` (the `plugin-grid` summary readers) — and the two merged spec files read as diffs, `packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts`, with `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` scanned for any summary, aggregate, view or grid line. The card, the records of rounds 1 to 3 and `delta-r4.md` were read. Nothing was built or run; only read-only git commands (`diff`, `log`, `rev-parse`, `merge-base`, `cmp`) were used.

### ① Derived judgments

- Round 4, a delta over round 1 (head `3fdcf28c`, FAIL), round 2 (head `45ec3be8`, PASS with three should-fixes) and round 3 (head `aa315089bac6f3915bf9334e744790e860cde42e`, PASS, nits only). The head moved to a merge commit: first parent `aa315089`, second parent `1af8253948` (the tip of `origin/main`, which is also the new merge base). No must-fix, no should-fix, no new nit.
- RIGHT — the PR's net diff is unchanged. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` at this head is byte-identical to the net diff at `aa315089` against its base `f0f729e71` (`cmp` of `net-aa.diff` and `net-merged.diff` reports no difference, and both were regenerated from git here and match the files). Same eight paths: the changeset and the seven `packages/lint/src` files in Scope.
- RIGHT — the merge is clean on the PR's paths. The 84 files the merge brought in and the 8 PR paths have an empty intersection; `git diff aa315089 HEAD` restricted to the 8 PR paths is empty, so no conflict resolution rewrote a line the earlier rounds judged.
- RIGHT — nothing the PR cites or depends on moved. `git diff aa315089 HEAD` is empty over `packages/lint`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/spec/src/ui`, `packages/spec/src/data` and `ui`. That covers the aggregate table, `isAggregateCompatibleWithFieldType`, `isMultiValueField`, `COLUMN_SUMMARY_AGGREGATION`, `VIRTUAL_FIELD_AGGREGATE_REMEDY` / `virtualFieldAggregateRemedy`, the engine aggregate door, the reference-integrity suite and its registration, the explain entries, and the `plugin-grid` summary readers.
- RIGHT — the six commits merged from main are on other surfaces: `os audit verify` and the audit seal verifier (#32473), `composeStacks` action-key collisions through nested artifacts (#32475), SSO provider read (#32464), `applySeedBodies` host (#32463), object-schema read visibility on the meta outlets (#32428), MCP tool refusal text (#32476).
- RIGHT — the four `packages/spec` files in the merge do not reach this PR. `suggestions.zod.ts` adds an optional `retiredKeyUpgradeGuide` to `strictUnknownKeyError`, default `true`, so every existing strict-key refusal reads as before; `protocol-upgrade-guide.ts` is a comment change; `stack.zod.ts` changes `composeStacks` collision reading and carries no summary, aggregate, view or grid line; `api/rest-server.zod.ts` is the REST server config. The PR's lint code calls none of them: its only mentions of `composeStacks` in `packages/lint/src` are prose in an unrelated rule.
- Round 3's nits are unchanged by the merge and are not re-graded: the "no exception" wording of the list-view message, the 41-character field-name room with `multiple: true`, the file-level `fired` recorder in the hint sweep, and the private predicate twin in `validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`.

### ② Semver level

- RIGHT — unchanged: `'@objectstack/lint': minor` with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the one ADR-0087 marker, as judged in round 3. The changeset file is byte-identical. The merge added seven changesets of its own for other packages; none names this PR's rule or alters its level, and the PR still holds exactly one changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) to (f) of round 3 stand as written: sibling rule id ACCEPT; `isMultiValueField` beside the table predicate ACCEPT; `aggregate-pair-verdict.ts` as an unexported lint-internal file ACCEPT; one-page ungrouped case RESOLVED by the seat's ruling; `object-grid` `properties.columns[].summary` OUT OF SCOPE by the seat's word and owed in the PR body; `VIRTUAL_FIELD_AGGREGATE_REMEDY` naming `count_distinct` ACCEPT. The merge touches none of the code behind them.
- No new boundary: the merge adds no second caller of the aggregate door, no new summary surface, and no new member to `COLUMN_SUMMARY_AGGREGATION`.

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing is the one round 3 judged, line for line: the door's refusal made real at authoring on list-view column summaries and object-grid aggregations, by the door's own two criteria, against a spec table and a door that are the same bytes at this head as at `aa315089`. The head move changes no verdict, no message, no hint and no explain text.
- Against the published spec on the new `origin/main`: the capability taken away and the three figures the author loses are as recorded and ruled in round 3; main gained nothing that restores or widens them, and nothing that makes a pair the lint refuses acceptable at the door.
- Owed by the PR body, unchanged from round 3: first-party counts on the final head, the `object-grid` column-summary residue, and the one line on the shared virtual-field remedy sentence.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c6230f4eeb0d099361dffba340f855a280a3334f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `202ae5248e9911d05394b81d766b675ac83f4ce7` — the merge of head `40e099dddaefb80710369d91011d851f004874e4` into base `c6230f4eeb0d099361dffba340f855a280a3334f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 202ae5248e9911d05394b81d766b675ac83f4ce7 && git checkout 202ae5248e9911d05394b81d766b675ac83f4ce7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c6230f4eeb0d099361dffba340f855a280a3334f 40e099dddaefb80710369d91011d851f004874e4 && git checkout -B drift-repro c6230f4eeb0d099361dffba340f855a280a3334f && git merge --no-ff 40e099dddaefb80710369d91011d851f004874e4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c6230f4eeb0d099361dffba340f855a280a3334f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c6230f4eeb0d099361dffba340f855a280a3334f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.
